docs.title: Sibyl 🔮
docs.text: An LLM-powered research paper review system that leverages local open-source AI models to provide comprehensive, comparative reviews of academic papers.

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
This repository is organized into two self-contained sub-projects:

Directory Description backend/ Python / FastAPI API server web/ Next.js frontend

Each sub-directory contains its own README.md, Dockerfile, and all files needed to develop, test, and deploy that component independently.

docs.title: Quick Start (Docker Compose)
docs.text:
The easiest way to run the full stack is with Docker Compose from the repository root:

# 1. Copy and edit the backend environment file
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env

# 2. Start all services (Ollama, GROBID, backend, frontend)
docker compose up -d

# 3. Pull a model into Ollama (first time only)
docker compose exec ollama ollama pull llama3.2

# 4. Open the web app
#    http://localhost:4000

docs.title: Backend (Python / FastAPI)
docs.text:
cd backend

# Install dependencies (requires uv)
uv sync --extra web --extra dev

# Start the API server
sibyl --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --log-level INFO

# Run tests
pytest

See backend/README.md for full documentation.

docs.title: Frontend (Next.js)
docs.text:
cd web

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start the development server
npm run dev

# Open http://localhost:3000

See web/README.md for full documentation.

docs.title: Contributing to Sibyl
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Sibyl! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository
  2. Clone your fork: git clone https://github.com/yourusername/sibyl.git
  3. Create a branch: git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
  4. Make your changes
  5. Test your changes
  6. Submit a pull request

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
# Install development dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Run tests
pytest

# Format code
black src/

# Check linting
ruff check src/

mypy src/

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• Follow PEP 8 guidelines
  • Use Black for formatting (line length: 100)
  • Add type hints to new functions
  • Write docstrings for public APIs

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Write tests for new features
  • Ensure all tests pass before submitting
  • Aim for good test coverage

docs.title: Pull Request Process
docs.text:
1. Update the README.md with details of changes if needed

  4. Your PR will be reviewed by maintainers

docs.title: Adding New LLM Providers
docs.text:
To add support for a new local LLM provider:

  1. Create a new client class in llm_client.py inheriting from LLMClient
  2. Implement the generate() and get_name() methods
  3. Add the provider to the factory function
  4. Update configuration in config.py
  5. Add tests
  6. Update documentation

Example for adding support for a hypothetical "LocalAI" provider:

class LocalAIClient(LLMClient):
    """Client for LocalAI models."""

    def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig):
        super().__init__(config)
        self.base_url = config.api_url or "http://localhost:8080"

    def generate(self, prompt: str, system_prompt: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
        """Generate a response using LocalAI's API."""
        # Implementation here
        pass

    def get_name(self) -> str:
        return f"LocalAI ({self.config.model})"

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text: Ensure you have: - Python 3.12 or higher (Python 3.12+ recommended for best compatibility) - uv - Fast Python package installer and resolver - Ollama installed and running locally - Node.js 18+ and npm (only if you want to use the web interface)

docs.title: 2. Install Ollama
docs.text:
Visit https://ollama.ai and download Ollama for your operating system.

Verify installation: 

ollama --version

docs.title: 3. Pull a Model
docs.text:
Download a local LLM model:

# Recommended: Llama 3.2 (good balance of speed and quality)
ollama pull llama3.2

# Or try other models:
ollama pull mistral         # Excellent reasoning
ollama pull phi3            # Small but powerful
ollama pull gemma2          # Google's efficient model
ollama pull qwen2.5         # Strong multilingual
ollama pull deepseek-coder  # Best for technical papers

Verify the model: 

ollama list

docs.title: 4. Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/cvasilatos/sibyl.git
cd sibyl

# Install uv if not already installed
# macOS and Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Windows
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# Install Sibyl
uv pip install -e .

# If you want the web interface, install with web dependencies:
uv pip install -e ".[web]"

docs.title: 5. Configure Sibyl
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and configure:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and set your model:

OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434

Optional: Enable GROBID for Better Metadata Extraction

If your PDFs don't have embedded metadata (title, authors), you can enable GROBID for automatic extraction:

# Start GROBID service using Docker
docker run -t --rm -p 8070:8070 lfoppiano/grobid:0.8.0

# In your .env file, add:
GROBID_ENABLED=true
GROBID_URL=http://localhost:8070

This is optional but recommended for academic papers without proper metadata.

docs.title: 6. Verify Setup
docs.text:
Check that everything is configured correctly:

sibyl check-config

You should see a table showing your configured model.

docs.title: 7. Review Your First Paper
docs.text:
sibyl review path/to/your/paper.pdf

That's it! Sibyl will: 1. Extract text from the PDF 2. Generate a review using your local LLM 3. Display structured feedback and scoring

docs.title: What Happens During a Review?
docs.text:
When you run sibyl review paper.pdf, here's what happens:

  1. PDF Parsing: Sibyl extracts text and metadata from your PDF
  2. Review Generation: Your configured local LLM reads the paper and provides:
  3. Assessment of novelty, methodology, results, clarity, and impact
  4. Identification of limitations and strengths
  5. Overall score (1-10)
  6. Recommendation (Accept/Revise/Reject)
  7. Detailed feedback
  8. Results Display: Sibyl displays the structured review with formatting

docs.title: Single Model Review
docs.text:
# Review with your configured model
sibyl review paper.pdf

docs.title: Compare Multiple Models
docs.text:
To compare different models, you can run reviews sequentially:

# Review with Llama
sibyl review paper.pdf -o review_llama.json

# Change model in .env to mistral, then:
sibyl review paper.pdf -o review_mistral.json

# For technical papers, try DeepSeek:
# Change model in .env to deepseek-coder, then:
sibyl review paper.pdf -o review_deepseek.json

# Compare the results manually

docs.title: Save Results for Later
docs.text:
# Save as formatted text
sibyl review paper.pdf -o review.txt

# Save as JSON for processing
sibyl review paper.pdf -o review.json

docs.title: Review Long Papers
docs.text:
# Limit to first 20 pages (to save processing time)
sibyl review paper.pdf --max-pages 20

docs.title: Review Scores
docs.text:
• 9-10: Exceptional - Major contribution to the field
  • 7-8: Strong - Accept with minor revisions
  • 5-6: Average - Major revisions needed
  • 3-4: Weak - Likely reject
  • 1-2: Poor - Reject

docs.title: Consensus
docs.text:
When comparing reviews from different models (run sequentially):

  • Strong consensus: Models agree (±1 point) - High confidence
  • Moderate consensus: Most models agree - Normal variation
  • Mixed/No consensus: Significant disagreement - Needs human judgment

docs.title: Tips for Best Results
docs.text:
1. Choose the right model: Larger models generally provide better quality
  2. Ensure sufficient resources: Models need adequate RAM/VRAM
  3. Start with smaller papers: Test with shorter papers first
  4. Save your results: Keep records for comparison over time
  5. Read the details: Scores are just summaries; the detailed feedback is most valuable

docs.title: "No local LLM configured"
docs.text: Make sure: - .env file exists in the project root - OLLAMA_MODEL is set in the .env file - Ollama is installed and running (ollama list should work) - You have pulled the model (ollama pull <model-name>)

docs.title: "Failed to connect to Ollama"
docs.text:
• Ensure Ollama is running: ollama serve (usually runs automatically)
  • Check the base URL in .env matches your Ollama setup
  • Default is http://localhost:11434

docs.title: "Error extracting PDF"
docs.text:
• Ensure the PDF is not encrypted or password-protected
  • Try using --max-pages to limit extraction
  • Check that the file path is correct
  • If PDF metadata is empty, consider enabling GROBID (see configuration section above)

docs.title: Slow Performance
docs.text: If reviews are taking too long: - Use a smaller model (e.g., llama3.2:1b instead of llama3.2:3b) - Reduce the number of pages with --max-pages - Ensure you have sufficient RAM for the model - Consider using GPU acceleration if available

docs.title: Review Structure
docs.text:
Each review includes:

  1. Novelty: Is the research original?
  2. Methodology: Are the methods sound?
  3. Results: Are findings significant?
  4. Clarity: Is it well-written?
  5. Impact: Will it contribute to the field?
  6. Limitations: What are the weaknesses?
  7. Strengths: What are the strong points?
  8. Score: Numerical rating (1-10)
  9. Recommendation: Accept, Revise, or Reject
  10. Detailed Feedback: Specific suggestions

docs.title: Interpreting Scores
docs.text:
• 9-10: Exceptional paper, significant contribution
  • 7-8: Strong paper, accept with minor revisions
  • 5-6: Average paper, major revisions needed
  • 3-4: Weak paper, likely reject
  • 1-2: Poor quality, reject

docs.title: Consensus Indicators
docs.text:
• Strong consensus: All models agree
  • Moderate consensus: Majority agreement
  • Mixed: Significant disagreement

docs.title: For Best Results
docs.text:
1. Choose appropriate models: Larger models provide more detailed analysis
  2. Optimize hardware: Ensure sufficient RAM for your chosen model
  3. Review incrementally: Start with abstracts/introductions before full papers
  4. Read detailed feedback: The most valuable insights are in the details
  5. Save results: Keep records for later comparison

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
1. Use appropriate model sizes: Match model to your hardware
  2. Limit pages for long papers: Use --max-pages for efficiency
  3. Consider quantized models: Use smaller quantizations (e.g., Q4) for speed
  4. Monitor resource usage: Keep an eye on RAM/CPU usage

docs.title: In a Research Workflow
docs.text:
# Review a draft before submission
sibyl review draft.pdf -o draft_review.json

# Compare with feedback after revisions
sibyl review revised.pdf -o revised_review.json

# Review all papers in a directory
for paper in papers/*.pdf; do
    sibyl review "$paper" -o "reviews/$(basename "$paper" .pdf)_review.txt"
done

import json

# Load review results
with open('review_results.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Extract scores

average_score = sum(scores) / len(scores)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Sibyl supports local open-source LLMs running via Ollama. This guide helps you understand the characteristics of different models and choose the best one for your needs.

docs.title: Llama 3.2 (Meta)
docs.text:
Models: llama3.2:1b, llama3.2:3b

Strengths: - Excellent general capabilities - Multiple size options for different hardware - Strong reasoning abilities - Well-optimized for local execution

Best For: - General academic paper review - Balanced performance and quality - Users with moderate hardware

Typical Characteristics: - Provides thorough, balanced analysis - Good at identifying both strengths and weaknesses - Reliable across different paper types

Hardware: - 1B: 8GB RAM minimum - 3B: 16GB RAM recommended

docs.title: Mistral (Mistral AI)
docs.text:
Model: mistral:7b

Strengths: - Excellent reasoning and analytical capabilities - Strong attention to technical details - Good at identifying subtle issues - Fast inference relative to size

Best For: - Technical papers requiring deep analysis - Complex methodologies - When detail-oriented feedback is crucial

Typical Characteristics: - Thorough and methodical reviews - May be more critical than other models - Excellent at logical reasoning

Hardware: 16GB RAM recommended, 32GB optimal

docs.title: Phi-3 (Microsoft)
docs.text:
Models: phi3:mini (3.8B), phi3:medium (14B)

Strengths: - Impressive performance for size - Efficient resource usage - Strong language understanding - Good general knowledge

Best For: - Users with limited hardware - Quick reviews - General assessment needs

Typical Characteristics: - Concise, focused reviews - Good balance of quality and speed - Efficient on consumer hardware

Hardware: - Mini: 8GB RAM - Medium: 24GB RAM

docs.title: Gemma 2 (Google)
docs.text:
Models: gemma2:2b, gemma2:9b

Strengths: - Well-balanced capabilities - Good instruction following - Efficient architecture - Strong performance across tasks

Best For: - General paper review - Multi-domain research - Balanced assessments

Typical Characteristics: - Balanced, fair reviews - Good contextual understanding - Reliable outputs

Hardware: - 2B: 8GB RAM - 9B: 16-24GB RAM

docs.title: Qwen 2.5 (Alibaba)
docs.text:
Models: Various sizes from 0.5B to 72B

Strengths: - Strong multilingual capabilities - Excellent reasoning abilities - Good at structured outputs - Multiple size options

Best For: - Papers in multiple languages - Complex reasoning tasks - Structured analysis needs

Typical Characteristics: - Detailed, structured reviews - Good at following complex instructions - Strong analytical capabilities

Hardware: Varies by size (8GB to 64GB+ RAM)

docs.title: DeepSeek Coder (DeepSeek)
docs.text:
Models: deepseek-coder:1.3b, deepseek-coder:6.7b, deepseek-coder:33b

Strengths: - Exceptional understanding of code and technical content - Strong performance on technical and computer science papers - Good at analyzing algorithms and implementations - Excellent code snippet comprehension

Best For: - Computer science papers - Papers with significant code components - Algorithm analysis - Technical documentation review

Typical Characteristics: - Thorough technical analysis - Strong understanding of programming concepts - Good at identifying implementation issues - Detailed code-related feedback

Hardware: - 1.3B: 8GB RAM - 6.7B: 16GB RAM - 33B: 64GB+ RAM

docs.title: When to Compare Multiple Models
docs.text:
Sequential Comparison Beneficial: - High-stakes decisions (acceptance/rejection) - Controversial or novel work - When diverse perspectives are valuable - For comprehensive evaluation

Single Model Sufficient: - Preliminary reviews of your own work - Quick quality checks - Informal assessments - When time/resources are limited

docs.title: Recommended Approaches
docs.text:
Best Quality: Mistral or Llama 3.2:3b - Highest quality reviews - Best for critical decisions - Requires adequate hardware

Balanced: Llama 3.2:1b or Phi-3 Mini - Good balance of quality and speed - Sufficient for most purposes - Works on modest hardware

Fast/Efficient: Phi-3 Mini or Gemma 2:2b - Quick turnaround - Lower resource requirements - Good for initial screening

docs.title: Score Tendencies
docs.text:
Different models may have different scoring tendencies:

  • Mistral: Tends toward detailed, critical analysis
  • Llama: Balanced, uses full score range
  • Phi-3: Concise, focused feedback
  • Gemma: Balanced and fair
  • Qwen: Structured, detailed responses
  • DeepSeek: Technical focus, excellent for code/algorithms

docs.title: Focus Areas
docs.text:
• Mistral: Heavy emphasis on methodology and rigor
  • Llama: Balanced across all criteria
  • Phi-3: Focuses on key issues
  • Gemma: Good at practical implications
  • Qwen: Strong on structured analysis
  • DeepSeek: Excels at technical and algorithmic content

docs.title: Model Selection Tips
docs.text:
1. Match hardware to model: Don't choose a model too large for your system
  2. Consider paper complexity: Use larger models for complex papers
  3. Experiment: Try different models to find what works for your domain
  4. Document preferences: Track which models work best for your field

docs.title: Optimizing for Your Needs
docs.text: For Speed: Phi-3 Mini, Gemma 2:2b, Llama 3.2:1b, DeepSeek 1.3b For Quality: Mistral, Llama 3.2:3b, Qwen (larger variants), DeepSeek 33b For Balance: Llama 3.2:3b, Gemma 2:9b, DeepSeek 6.7b For Limited Hardware: Phi-3 Mini, Llama 3.2:1b, DeepSeek 1.3b For Technical Papers: DeepSeek Coder (any size), Mistral

docs.title: GPU Acceleration
docs.text: Models run significantly faster with GPU acceleration: - NVIDIA GPUs: Best support via CUDA - Apple Silicon: Good support via Metal - AMD GPUs: Growing support via ROCm

docs.title: Memory Requirements
docs.text: Approximate RAM needed (for Q4 quantization): - 1-2B models: 4-8GB - 3-4B models: 8-12GB - 7-8B models: 12-20GB - 13-14B models: 24-32GB - 30B+ models: 64GB+

docs.title: Future Model Support
docs.text: Ollama regularly adds support for new models. Check ollama list for available models or visit ollama.ai/library for the complete list.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The best model depends on your specific needs, hardware constraints, and use case. Start with Llama 3.2 or Phi-3 Mini to understand their characteristics, then experiment with others based on your requirements.

docs.title: Sibyl Storage and Search
docs.text: Sibyl now includes a powerful vector database storage system that allows you to save, organize, and semantically search through your research paper reviews.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The storage system uses ChromaDB, a vector database optimized for semantic search. Unlike traditional keyword search, vector search understands the meaning of your queries, enabling you to find papers based on concepts rather than exact word matches.

docs.title: 🔍 Semantic Search
docs.text: Search for papers by meaning, not just keywords: - Query: "papers about machine learning" - Finds: Papers about "neural networks", "deep learning", "ML algorithms", etc.

docs.title: 📊 Statistics Dashboard
docs.text: Track your review library with: - Total number of reviews - Average review scores - Number of unique papers reviewed - Recommendation distribution (Accept/Revise/Reject)

docs.title: 💾 Persistent Storage
docs.text:
• Reviews automatically saved after completion
  • PDFs stored alongside review metadata
  • Full review criteria and feedback preserved
  • Searchable by paper content and review details

docs.title: 🎯 Similarity Scoring
docs.text: Search results include similarity scores showing how closely each result matches your query.

docs.title: 1. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
# Install uv if not already installed
# macOS and Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Windows
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# Install Sibyl with web dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[web]"

docs.title: 2. (Optional) Install Ollama Embedding Model
docs.text:
For production-quality semantic search, install the embedding model:

ollama pull nomic-embed-text

Note: Sibyl will work without this, using a fallback embedding method for testing.

docs.title: 3. Start the Backend and Frontend
docs.text:
Terminal 1 - Backend: 

sibyl web

Terminal 2 - Frontend: 

cd web
npm install  # First time only
npm run dev

docs.text: Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

docs.title: Review Paper Tab
docs.text:
1. Upload a PDF research paper
  2. Click "Start Review" to analyze the paper
  3. View the generated review
  4. Review is automatically saved to your library

docs.title: Search Library Tab
docs.text:
1. View statistics about your review collection
  2. Enter a search query (e.g., "quantum computing", "neural networks")
  3. Click "Search Reviews" to find relevant papers
  4. Click on any result to view the full review

docs.title: API Usage
docs.text:
You can also use the storage system programmatically:

from sibyl.storage import ReviewStorage
from sibyl.reviewer import ReviewSystem, PaperReview
from sibyl.llm_client import create_client
from sibyl.config import SibylConfig

# Initialize storage
storage = ReviewStorage(storage_path="./sibyl_storage")

# After generating a review...
review_id = storage.save_review(
    review=paper_review,
    pdf_filename="my_paper.pdf",
    pdf_path="/path/to/my_paper.pdf",
    paper_text=extracted_paper_text
)

# Search for papers
results = storage.search_reviews("neural networks", limit=10)
for review in results:
    print(f"{review.paper_title}: {review.similarity_score:.2%} match")
    print(f"Score: {review.overall_score}/10")
    print(f"Recommendation: {review.recommendation}")
    print()

# Get a specific review
review_details = storage.get_review(review_id)
print(review_details["criteria"]["detailed_feedback"])

# List all reviews
all_reviews = storage.list_reviews(limit=50, offset=0)

# Get statistics
stats = storage.get_statistics()
print(f"Total reviews: {stats['total_reviews']}")
print(f"Average score: {stats['avg_score']:.1f}")
print(f"Unique papers: {stats['unique_papers']}")

# Delete a review
storage.delete_review(review_id)

docs.title: 1. Embedding Generation
docs.text: When you save a review, Sibyl creates a vector embedding - a numerical representation that captures the semantic meaning of: - Paper title - Review criteria (novelty, methodology, results, etc.) - Paper content (if provided)

docs.title: 2. Similarity Matching
docs.text: When you search, Sibyl: 1. Generates an embedding for your query 2. Compares it to all stored review embeddings 3. Ranks results by similarity (cosine distance) 4. Returns the most relevant matches

docs.title: 3. Example
docs.text:
Query: "papers about transformers"

Matches: - Papers explicitly about "transformers" ✓ - Papers about "attention mechanisms" ✓ (related concept) - Papers about "BERT" or "GPT" ✓ (transformer-based models) - Papers about "sequence-to-sequence models" ✓ (related architecture)

Traditional keyword search would miss most of these!

docs.title: Storage Location
docs.text:
All data is stored in the sibyl_storage/ directory:

sibyl_storage/
├── chromadb/          # Vector database files
└── pdfs/              # Stored PDF files

This directory is excluded from git by default.

docs.title: Custom Storage Path
docs.text: storage = ReviewStorage(storage_path="/path/to/my/storage")

docs.title: Custom Ollama URL
docs.text:
storage = ReviewStorage(
    storage_path="./sibyl_storage",
    ollama_url="http://192.168.1.100:11434"
)

docs.title: 1. Include Paper Text for Better Search
docs.text:
When saving reviews, include the full paper text:

storage.save_review(
    review=review,
    pdf_filename="paper.pdf",
    pdf_path="/path/to/paper.pdf",
    paper_text=full_extracted_text  # Important!
)

This significantly improves search quality by including paper content in embeddings.

docs.title: 2. Use Descriptive Search Queries
docs.text: Better queries lead to better results: - ❌ "ML" → ✓ "machine learning algorithms" - ❌ "NLP" → ✓ "natural language processing" - ❌ "papers" → ✓ "papers about sentiment analysis"

docs.title: 3. Check Similarity Scores
docs.text: Results with similarity > 0.7 are usually highly relevant. Results with similarity < 0.5 may be false positives.

docs.title: 4. Regular Cleanup
docs.text: As your library grows, periodically: - Delete outdated or superseded reviews - Merge duplicate reviews of the same paper - Archive old reviews to a backup location

docs.title: "No reviews found" when reviews exist
docs.text:
Cause: Embeddings may not have been generated properly.

Solution: 1. Check if Ollama is running: curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags 2. Install embedding model: ollama pull nomic-embed-text 3. Restart the Sibyl web server

docs.title: Slow search performance
docs.text:
Cause: Large number of reviews or slow embedding generation.

Solutions: - Limit search results with the limit parameter - Use more specific queries - Consider running Ollama on GPU for faster embeddings

docs.title: Storage directory growing too large
docs.text:
Cause: Many PDFs and reviews stored.

Solutions: - Delete old or unnecessary reviews via API - Use storage.delete_review(review_id) to remove specific reviews - Manually clean up the sibyl_storage/pdfs/ directory

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
For large libraries, use pagination:

# Get first page (reviews 0-49)
page1 = storage.list_reviews(limit=50, offset=0)

# Get second page (reviews 50-99)
page2 = storage.list_reviews(limit=50, offset=50)

docs.title: Filtering by Score
docs.text:
# Get all reviews
reviews = storage.list_reviews(limit=1000)

# Filter high-scoring papers
high_quality = [r for r in reviews if r.overall_score >= 8]

# Filter by recommendation
accepted = [r for r in reviews if r.recommendation == "Accept"]

docs.title: Export Reviews
docs.text:
import json

# Get all reviews
reviews = storage.list_reviews(limit=1000)

# Export to JSON
export_data = [
    {
        "id": r.id,
        "title": r.paper_title,
        "score": r.overall_score,
        "recommendation": r.recommendation,
        "filename": r.pdf_filename,
        "created_at": r.created_at,
    }
    for r in reviews
]

with open("reviews_export.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(export_data, f, indent=2)

docs.title: Comparison: Vector vs. Keyword Search
docs.text: Feature Keyword Search (SQLite FTS) Vector Search (ChromaDB) Matches exact words ✓ ✓ Understands synonyms ✗ ✓ Finds related concepts ✗ ✓ Handles typos Limited ✓ Multilingual Limited ✓ Ranks by relevance Basic Advanced Similarity scores ✗ ✓ Setup complexity Low Medium

docs.title: WebSocket for Real-time Updates
docs.text:
import asyncio
import websockets
import json

async def review_paper(session_id):
    uri = f"ws://localhost:8000/ws/{session_id}"

    async with websockets.connect(uri) as websocket:
        while True:
            message = await websocket.recv()
            data = json.loads(message)

            if data["status"] == "progress":
                print(f"{data['progress']}%: {data['message']}")

            elif data["status"] == "completed":
                print("Review complete!")
                results = data["results"]
                print(f"Paper: {results['paper_title']}")
                print(f"Reviews: {len(results['reviews'])}")
                break

            elif data["status"] == "error":
                print(f"Error: {data['message']}")
                break

# Usage
asyncio.run(review_paper("your-session-id"))

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Sibyl Web Application has been refactored to use modern web technologies:

  • Next.js 15 - React framework with App Router
  • React 19 - UI library for component-based development
  • TypeScript - Type-safe development
  • Tailwind CSS - Utility-first CSS framework
  • shadcn/ui - High-quality component library built on Radix UI

docs.title: Frontend (Next.js)
docs.text:
• Located in /web directory
  • Runs on http://localhost:3000 by default
  • Communicates with FastAPI backend via REST API and WebSocket

docs.title: Backend (FastAPI)
docs.text:
• Located in /src/sibyl/web_app.py
  • Runs on http://localhost:8000
  • Provides REST API endpoints and WebSocket for real-time updates
  • CORS enabled for Next.js frontend

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+ (Python 3.12+ recommended) with Sibyl installed
  • uv - Fast Python package installer
  • Node.js 18+ and npm
  • Ollama installed and running with a model pulled

  • Before: No type safety

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Sibyl Web Application provides a FastAPI backend for the web interface. This document covers the backend server. For the Next.js frontend, see WEB_APP_NEXTJS.md.

The backend is built with FastAPI and provides: - REST API endpoints for file uploads, reviews, and health checks - WebSocket support for real-time progress updates - CORS enabled for Next.js frontend running on port 3000

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 📤 Drag & Drop Upload: Easy PDF file upload with drag-and-drop support
  • ⚡ Real-time Updates: WebSocket-based progress tracking during review
  • 🎨 Modern UI: Clean, responsive design that works on desktop and mobile
  • 📊 Comparative Analysis: View statistics and consensus across reviews
  • 🔒 Privacy-First: All processing happens locally - no data leaves your machine
  • 💰 Zero Cost: Completely free to use with local LLM models

docs.title: Command Line Options
docs.text:
Start the web server with custom host and port:

# Default (0.0.0.0:8000)
sibyl web

# Custom host and port
sibyl web --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# Enable SSL with self-signed certificate
sibyl web --ssl

# Help
sibyl web --help

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text: The backend provides the following REST API endpoints for the Next.js frontend:

docs.title: GET /api/health
docs.text:
Health check endpoint to verify service status.

Response: 

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "providers": ["ollama"],
  "ollama_base_url": "http://localhost:11434"
}

docs.title: POST /api/upload
docs.text:
Upload a PDF file for review.

Request: - Form data with file field containing PDF

Response: 

{
  "session_id": "uuid-string",
  "filename": "paper.pdf"
}

docs.title: GET /api/session/{session_id}
docs.text:
Get the status of a review session.

Response: 

{
  "session_id": "uuid-string",
  "status": "processing",
  "progress": 50,
  "message": "Reviewing with ollama...",
  "paper_title": "Research Paper Title"
}

docs.title: WebSocket /ws/{session_id}
docs.text:
WebSocket endpoint for real-time review progress updates.

Messages: 

// Progress update
{
  "status": "progress",
  "progress": 50,
  "message": "Generating review..."
}

// Completion
{
  "status": "completed",
  "progress": 100,
  "message": "Review complete!",
  "results": {
    "paper_title": "...",
    "reviews": [...],
    "comparison": {...}
  }
}

// Error
{
  "status": "error",
  "message": "Error description"
}

docs.title: Backend (FastAPI)
docs.text:
• FastAPI: Modern, fast web framework with automatic API documentation
  • Uvicorn: Lightning-fast ASGI server
  • WebSockets: Real-time bidirectional communication
  • Pydantic: Data validation and settings management

docs.title: Frontend (Next.js)
docs.text:
• Next.js 15: React framework with App Router
  • React 19: UI library for component-based development
  • TypeScript: Type-safe development
  • Tailwind CSS: Utility-first CSS framework
  • shadcn/ui: High-quality component library
  • WebSocket Client: Real-time progress updates

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. User uploads PDF via web interface
  2. File is saved temporarily with unique session ID
  3. WebSocket connection established for progress updates
  4. PDF text extracted
  5. LLM generates review (progress updates sent via WebSocket)
  6. Results displayed in web interface
  7. Temporary file cleaned up

docs.title: Running in Development Mode
docs.text:
# Install development dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[dev,web]"

# Run with auto-reload
uvicorn sibyl.web_app:app --reload --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
# Run web app tests
pytest tests/test_web_app.py -v

# Run all tests
pytest -v

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• File Validation: Only PDF files are accepted
  • Session Management: Unique session IDs prevent conflicts
  • Temporary Files: Automatically cleaned up after processing
  • XSS Prevention: All user content is escaped in the UI
  • Local Processing: No data sent to external services

docs.title: Server won't start
docs.text:
Issue: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi'

Solution: Install web dependencies 

uv pip install -e ".[web]"

docs.title: Can't connect to Ollama
docs.text:
Issue: Health check shows "unhealthy"

Solution: 1. Ensure Ollama is running: ollama list 2. Check .env configuration 3. Verify OLLAMA_BASE_URL is correct

docs.title: WebSocket connection fails
docs.text:
Issue: Connection error in browser console

Solution: 1. Check firewall settings 2. Ensure WebSocket traffic is allowed 3. Try using --host 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0

docs.title: Review takes too long
docs.text:
Issue: Process seems stuck

Solution: 1. Check system resources (CPU/RAM) 2. Try a smaller model (e.g., llama3.2:1b) 3. Limit pages with --max-pages option 4. Check Ollama logs: journalctl -u ollama -f

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Use Appropriate Models:
  2. 8GB RAM: llama3.2:1b, phi3:mini
  3. 16GB RAM: llama3.2:3b, mistral:7b

  4. 32GB+ RAM: Larger models

  5. Limit Page Count:

  6. For testing, use --max-pages 5

  7. For full reviews, use all pages

  8. GPU Acceleration:

  9. Ollama automatically uses GPU if available
  10. Check with: nvidia-smi (NVIDIA) or rocm-smi (AMD)
